result.headline: Rays vision with depth 4 barely moved DQN: its test mean rose only from 26.51 to 27.06 (+0.6, within single-seed noise), and its body crashes fell from 76% to 69% of test games.
result.summary:
DQN (the Q-learning agent that learns the value of each move from stored experience) reached a test mean of 27.06 (median 28, best 44) over 100 fixed-seed games. It ended 69 games by hitting its body, 31 by hitting a wall and none by starving. It averaged 240 steps per game and 9 steps per apple, so it is efficient and quick to die rather than wandering. Its training curve climbed quickly: mean of the last 100 games was about 16 after 0.9 minutes (110k steps), then hovered between 19 and 21 for the remaining four minutes, ending at 20.64. That is a plateau, not a steady climb. The training mean includes exploration (random moves that DQN still takes), so the test score is the better measure.

The GA (genetic algorithm: a population of networks that are mutated and selected, with no gradients) reached a test mean of 25.05 (median 26, best 31). It ended 86 games by body collision, 11 by wall and 3 by starvation, with 559 steps per game and 22 steps per apple. Its curve rose to about 16 by 1.2 minutes and then stayed flat around 15 to 17 for the rest of the run, ending at 16.67. It ran about 66 million environment steps, against 0.47 million for DQN, because it uses 11 cores in parallel. Its test mean fell 5.4 points from the window run (30.49 to 25.05), which is the largest change in this comparison. With one seed, that could be noise, since GA results vary from one population draw to the next.
result.diagnosis: The longer sight lines did not give DQN a clear advantage, which suggests that seeing four squares along a line is not the missing piece. Both vision types already show the nearest body part on the nearby squares, so the snake was not blind to its own body. On a 10x10 board, a snake of about 25 to 30 segments fills a large share of the space, and most deaths probably come from boxing itself in several moves ahead, which neither vision reports directly. The 5-minute budget gave DQN only 471k steps, and its curve had flattened, so a reward or time change may matter more than vision here. The GA's drop is probably seed noise, or the best-model choice for the test, because its training mean was unchanged (16.71 vs 16.67) while its test score moved by 5 points.
result.learned: Changing the sensor only helps if the crashes come from information the sensor lacks; here DQN still dies from its own body with almost the same frequency. Always read the test mean together with how the games ended and against the spread of a single seed.
result.prediction_check: Mostly missed: DQN's mean moved 0.6 points (predicted more than 3), its body share fell to 69%, just under the predicted 70% bar, and the GA changed more than DQN (-5.4 vs +0.6), the opposite of the prediction.

recommendations.title: Raise the death penalty to 30
recommendations.why: DQN still crashes into its body in 69% of test games, so if the penalty for crashing is too weak to teach avoidance, a stronger one should cut body crashes. This tests whether the problem is the reward signal rather than the sight.
recommendations.change: Set the death penalty from 10 to 30 and keep rays depth 4, the other reward features, and the 5-minute budget.
recommendations.prediction: DQN's body-crash share drops below 60% (from 69%), and its test mean stays between 24 and 30.
recommendations.question: Does a stronger death penalty make DQN avoid its body more, and does that raise its score?

recommendations.title: Extend rays to depth 8
recommendations.why: Depth 4 gave no gain over the 2-square window, but on a 10x10 board a longer sight line may still reveal a body segment or wall that depth 4 misses. This checks whether the sight range is the limit at all.
recommendations.change: Set rays depth from 4 to 8 and keep the reward and the 5-minute budget.
recommendations.prediction: DQN's test mean stays within 3 points of 27.06 (between 24 and 30), and its body-crash share stays between 60% and 75%.
recommendations.question: Is a much longer sight range useful, or is seeing four squares already enough?

recommendations.title: Train for 10 minutes instead of 5
recommendations.why: DQN's training curve flattened at about 20 after 2 minutes, so more time may not help. Doubling the budget tests whether DQN is still learning or has stopped.
recommendations.change: Set the time budget from 5 to 10 minutes and keep rays depth 4 and the reward.
recommendations.prediction: DQN's test mean rises by less than 3 points (stays below about 30), because its training curve was already flat by minute 2.3.
recommendations.question: Does DQN keep improving with more time, or has it reached its ceiling with this setup?

ideas.title: Free-space flood-fill vision feature
ideas.what: Add a vision input that reports how many empty squares the snake can reach from its head without crossing its body or a wall, perhaps split into the left, straight and right options. This gives the network a direct sense of boxing itself in.
ideas.why: Both the window and rays visions still show DQN dying from its own body in 69 to 76% of test games, even though each sees the nearby body. Neither reports how much room is left, which is what matters when the snake grows long on a small board.
ideas.expected: DQN's body-crash share falls by 10 points or more (from 69% to 60% or lower), and its test mean rises by 3 or more points.
